newsitem.title: USA: Clinton reaffirms U.S. support for Zaire mission.
newsitem.headline: Clinton reaffirms U.S. support for Zaire mission.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday reports that Rwandan refugees were streaming home from Zaire were "a hopeful sign" but the United States remains prepared to contribute troops to an international relief mission.

"The world's most powerful nation must not turn its back on so many desperate people and so many innocent children ...," Clinton said at a news conference. "The mission Canada proposes to lead, and that I believe America should take part in, would provide security for civilian relief agencies to deliver the aid these people must have and to help the refugees who so desire to return home to Rwanda."

Washington announced earlier this week it had agreed tentatively to send 1,000 troops to Goma, Zaire, to secure the airport and set up a protected corridor so refugees can return to Rwanda, with another 3,000 U.S. troops or so providing support from neighbouring countries.

Reports of a sudden mass movement of Rwandan refugees toward home raised questions of whether this might eliminate the need for an international relief mission, but Clinton said it would be premature to draw any such conclusion.

"I think we have to be prepared for the prospect that we will still have to have some presence there to facilitate this (relief operation) and to make sure as quickly as possible (to) get everything that is needed to them," he said. "... It's a hopeful sign but that's about all I can say right now," he said of the refugee movement reports

The United States has said its commitment was conditioned upon getting satisfactory assurances on the scope and duration of the mission, among other things. Clinton added nothing on that issue in his news conference remarks.
